Title: 'Empower communities, build trust to ensure disaster preparedness' - Dr Mexmollen Marcus
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: When an earthquake with a magnitude of 6.0 struck Mount Kinabalu on June 5, 2015, Dr Mexmollen Marcus learned that there were serious gaps in the authorities' response to such a disaster.
Recalling his experience as an on-call junior doctor who was stranded at Panalaban for three days following the earthquake, he said emergency response was severely hampered by bad weather and the lack of previous joint disaster exercises.
"I saw the helicopters that came to try to save us every time they came over, but they couldn't land because of bad weather.
"I did what I knew I had to do, which was to treat the sick. The armed forces did what they needed to do, which was probably to control the situation.
"The police did their own thing, the fire department did their own thing, so in the end we were very fragmented.
"Mountain guides, who knew the terrain intimately, became crucial first responders by carrying injured climbers down the mountain and searching for those who were missing, as they knew each ridge and every gully because they walked that same road on the mountain for a living," he said, adding that
18 people
, including students, were killed in the incident.
Dr Mexmollen was delivering his keynote speech at the Pacific Partnership 2026 (PP26) Symposium: Forging Partnerships and Advancing Health: A Global Perspective at INTAN Sabah here yesterday.
The Universiti Malaysia Sabah Faculty of Medicine deputy dean added that poor communication and information-sharing, lack of trust, unclear roles and fragmented governance were among the recurring weaknesses in disaster response.
He said the most important solution was to build trust between agencies rather than attempting to establish working relationships only when a crisis occurred.
"Trust is the precondition, not the outcome. It is not built when the crisis is here. Trust is built here, in a place where we can sit down and talk to each other clearly in peace," he said.
He also called for communities to be placed at the centre of disaster preparedness, saying local residents were often the natural first responders and their traditional knowledge should be incorporated into early warning systems.
Looking ahead, he said Malaysia must strengthen the link between health security and disaster governance, particularly as future emergencies could involve multiple hazards occurring simultaneously.
"Our hazards have merged. Our task starting now is to make certain that we do too.
"The next biological hazard will in all likelihood cross from animals to humans long before it actually reaches our hospitals," he said, adding that there should be emphasis on the multidisciplinary One Health approach to tackle zoonotic diseases.
Meanwhile, PP26 mission commander Captain Robert Reyes said the core reason for the partnership was not for the multinational partners to forge relationships only at the scene of a disaster.
"We need to do that now. These subject matter expert exchanges (for two days) are part of that greater purpose so that the connections and relationships you build here will endure for many, many years to come."
PP26 medical operations director Captain Tiffany Uranga said the symposium aims to deepen our mutual understanding of how military and civilian entities can seamlessly integrate to save lives, build human connections and bolster regional capacity for non-traditional threats.
"To effectively integrate our efforts, we must commit to a comprehensive, whole-of-society approach. This is why our agenda over these two days is intentionally structured around multidisciplinary readiness."
Present was PP26 exercise director Colonel Ismail Mohamed.

Title: Azeez Rahim to face corruption charge today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim will first be brought before the Sessions Court for a separate remand proceeding before facing a corruption charge today.

Title: 25 years after 9/11, Americans fear domestic extremists more than foreign attacks: Poll
Article:
WASHINGTON: Twenty-five years after the Sept 11 attacks focused US fears on threats from abroad, Americans are now considerably more worried about attacks by domestic extremists than by foreign groups, a Reuters/Ipsos poll found.
When asked to name the biggest threat to the safety of average Americans, 33 per cent of respondents picked "domestic terrorism," while 20 per cent picked foreign terror and 42 per cent pointed to random acts of violence such as mass shootings, the Aug 28-31 poll found.
The picture was much different a decade ago. Reuters/Ipsos polling from mid-2013 showed 21 per cent of Americans viewed domestic terror as the top threat, less than the 28 per cent who pointed to foreign terror and 51 per cent who picked random acts of violence.
Foreign al Qaeda militants crashed airplanes into New York City's World Trade Center and the Pentagon outside Washington on Sept 11, 2001, killing thousands and sparking decades of war, including the US-led invasion of Afghanistan, where al Qaeda leaders were based.
Al Qaeda also inspired the 2013 Boston Marathon bombing, in which a pair of foreign-born brothers killed three and injured more than 260, with a fourth person killed a few days later.
But the US has also seen many domestically inspired attacks, including the 2016 mass shooting that killed 49 people at a Florida gay nightclub and other attacks on Black, Latino or Jewish Americans.
President Donald Trump himself faced multiple assassination attempts, including a 2024 shooting that wounded his ear, and conservative activist Charlie Kirk was gunned down in September 2025 while speaking to university students in Utah.
Asked which ideology-driven attacks pose the bigger threat, 61 per cent of respondents in the latest poll picked domestic extremists and 34 per cent picked those from abroad.
The legacy of the Sept 11 attacks remains strong, the survey found. Six in 10 people say they periodically think about the attacks and roughly the same share say they would support a military response if there were another major attack.
But Americans do not believe that wars that followed 9/11 were worth the cost. Some 48 per cent said the war in Afghanistan was not worth its toll, compared with 21 per cent who said it was, while the rest were unsure or didn't answer the question.
The war in Iraq was similarly unpopular, with 51 per cent disapproving and 21 per cent approving.
Public disapproval of those wars played a role in Trump's rise, as he campaigned on a platform of avoiding enduring wars.
Trump himself launched a war on Iran six months ago that has eluded efforts for a speedy resolution.
The poll found only 25 per cent of Americans think the conflict has been worth it, compared with 54 per cent who think it hasn't been.
Six in 10 Americans - including eight in 10 Republicans - think the US government response to the Sept 11 attacks has been at least somewhat effective in preventing attacks against Americans on US soil.
A bipartisan majority - including 71 per cent of Democrats and 75 per cent of Republicans - think the beefed-up airport security that took hold following the Sept 11 attacks has been worth the disruptions to people's trips.
Americans are also more inclined to support government-run airport security, with only 23 per cent supporting an idea studied by the Trump administration that would replace federal security with private contractors.
Forty-eight per cent were opposed, the poll found.
The expansion of domestic surveillance after 2001 has been less popular, with 65 per cent opposed to allowing US intelligence agencies to monitor electronic communications of US citizens without a warrant.
A 2008 law that allowed that to happen lapsed in June, though the Trump administration has asked Congress to reauthorise the practice.
The Reuters/Ipsos poll, which was conducted online, surveyed 1,167 US adults nationwide, with margins of error between 3 and 6 percentage points.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sarawak helicopter crash: Air accident investigators to arrive in Miri today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Air Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) team is expected to arrive in Miri today to begin investigating the helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Sarawak.
Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) chief executive officer Datuk Captain Norazman Mahmud said the team is expected to arrive in Miri at 2pm before assisting with the investigation into the crash.
"The helicopter wreckage at the crash site will remain undisturbed following instructions from the AAIB... the site has been cordoned off and secured.
"Meanwhile, authorities will resume search and recovery operations at the crash site today," he told the New Straits Times.
Norazman said a Fire and Rescue Department helicopter carrying 18 personnel from various agencies departed Miri for Long Lellang at 7am.
Two police helicopters would follow at 10am, with one departing Kuching carrying five personnel and another from Kota Kinabalu carrying six personnel, both from Miri.
"Four police personnel from Long Lama and four Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency personnel from Miri are also en route to Long Lellang," he said.
Norazman said police would manage the identification and investigation process at Miri Hospital, including comparing the victims' DNA with that of their families.
He added that the Long Lellang runway had been closed to fixed-wing aircraft, with a Notice to Airmen issued and activated.
Yesterday, the CAAM said a
Flying Doctor Service Bo-105 helicopter
carrying five people crashed near the Long Lellang STOLport in Sarawak.
It said that it received notification of the incident from the Flight Information Service at 3.58pm.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit opens higher against US dollar amid rate-hike expectations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Wednesday as the greenback weakened, while markets weighed the prospects of interest rate hikes in the United States and Japan.
At 8am, the local currency strengthened to 4.0560/0635 against the greenback from Tuesday's close of 4.0605/0640.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said higher US Treasury yields suggested that the Federal Reserve could opt for a higher benchmark interest rate when the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meets on Sept 15-16.
"The US Treasury notes auction for three-month and six-month bills yielded higher at 3.80 per cent and 3.89 per cent, respectively," he told Bernama.
Mohd Afzanizam also said the Japanese yen strengthened against the US dollar to 153.53 yen, reflecting growing expectations that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) could raise its policy rate, supported by signs of stronger economic performance.
He said the BOJ could raise its policy rate by 25 basis points on Sept 18 as the economy showed healthy growth alongside rising inflation, which stood at 1.9 per cent in July.
"Japan's second quarter of 2026 gross domestic product came in higher than expected at a 1.4 per cent quarter-on-quarter annualised rate, versus consensus estimates of 1.1 per cent.
"In addition, wage growth among Japanese employees accelerated further to 4.7 per cent year-on-year in July, against market expectations of 3.9 per cent," he said.
Meanwhile, Quintex Intel global strategist Stephen Innes said currency markets were treating an expected Fed rate move largely as an insurance hike rather than the start of a sustained tightening cycle.
"Investors' view is that this could be reversed fairly quickly once West Asia tensions ease and oil settles back towards the mid-US$80s per barrel, which may increasingly be viewed as the new normal," he added.
The ringgit traded lower against most major currencies.
It slipped against the Japanese yen to 2.6437/6488 from 2.6374/6398 at Tuesday's close, fell against the euro to 4.7167/7254 from 4.7151/7191, and eased against the British pound to 5.4934/5036 from 5.4926/4974.
Against regional currencies, the ringgit traded mostly higher.
It edged up against the Thai baht to 12.3241/3529 from 12.3285/3447 at the previous close, strengthened against the Philippine peso to 6.47/6.49 from 6.48/6.49, and rose against the Indonesian rupiah to 230.0/230.5 from 230.3/230.5 previously.
However, the local note softened against the Singapore dollar to 3.2081/2143 from 3.2073/2104 previously.

Title: Oil prices climb as Mideast war flares
Article:
AFP
HONG KONG: Oil prices climbed on Wednesday to near US$100 a barrel in early Asia trade, as war in the Middle East threatened to further choke supply from the crude-rich region.
The price of Brent crude, the benchmark international contract, rose to US$99.38 per barrel, while the main US contract West Texas Intermediate was at US$94.51 per barrel.
Iran said on Wednesday it struck a US military base in Jordan and that it would target oil tankers off Kuwait and Bahrain in retaliation for US strikes on its vessels.

Title: Wall Street down, oil up as inflation, Middle East worries persist
Article:
WASHINGTON: Stocks slipped on Tuesday and oil flirted with US$100 a barrel prices as investors fretted over potential inflation concerns and ongoing conflict in the Middle East.
All three major US indices dipped Tuesday, kicking off a holiday-shortened week on a lower note. The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed down 1.18 per cent, while the S&P 500 dropped 0.58 per cent and the Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.32 per cent.
MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe was last down 0.55 per cent.
Meanwhile, oil prices climbed after Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen attacked Saudi energy facilities. Brent crude oil was up 2.13 per cent to US$99.07 a barrel and US crude jumped 2.82 per cent to US$94.05 a barrel.
A resurgence in inflation has knocked the equity market in the past few weeks, in large part because of the surge in bond yields to multi-year highs, which puts central banks under pressure to raise interest rates.
The European Central Bank is all but certain to raise euro zone rates by a quarter point on Thursday this week, while the chances of the Bank of Japan doing the same next week are intensifying, which has set the yen on course for its strongest rally in two years. The Federal Reserve is also set to reconsider its rates, issuing a new statement on September 16.
US inflation data on Friday could prove decisive in setting expectations for the outcome of the Fed's upcoming meeting. Right now, money markets show traders are attaching a roughly 58 per cent chance of a rate rise.
Oil remained the dominant theme on Tuesday, but the yen's surge looms large for global markets. Because of its status as a low-yielding currency, traders have borrowed yen in earnest to fund purchases of higher-yielding assets across currencies, bonds and equities, a strategy known as the carry trade.
In the last week alone, the yen has gained nearly four per cent, its largest week-on-week increase since July 2024. On Tuesday, it was trading around 153.97, leaving the dollar slightly lower on the day.
The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, including the yen and the euro, rose 0.02 per cent to 98.86.
In commodities beyond oil, the price of copper hit a record high on Tuesday, as global supply tightened with the metal continuing to flow into the US ahead of possible tariffs.
Three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange was up 1.5 per cent at US$14,728 a ton.
In the bond market, benchmark US 10-year Treasury notes were yielding 4.8 per cent, not far off their highest since November 2023.

Title: A community brought together through faith and prayers [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: For residents of Taman Bukit Maluri, the annual Hungry Ghost Festival is more than a religious observance.
It has become a celebration that brings the local community together while preserving traditions passed down through generations.
At the annual Hungry Ghost Festival celebration organised by Persatuan Yee Lan Guan Yin Ting Bukit Maluri Kepong at the Guan Yin Ting temple, preparations began more than two months ago.
Observed during the seventh month of the lunar calendar, the Hungry Ghost Festival, known as Phor Thor in Hokkien and Yu Lan in Mandarin, is widely celebrated across East and Southeast Asia.
According to Taoist belief, the Gates of Hell will open during this period, allowing spirits to roam freely among the living.
The association, established in 1982, has continued the annual tradition among devotees in the area, with the festival held on the 26th day of the seventh month of the lunar calendar.
The association's secretary, Cheah Hong Kee, said the festival welcomes anyone who wishes to pray with a sincere heart.
"Besides preserving our faith and culture, this annual celebration naturally brings people together.
"Our main intention is to uphold our faith — praying to the deities for peace and well-being for everyone," the 78-year-old said.
Cheah said the temple also holds a ceremonial dinner the following day, a tradition that has evolved from practices observed by previous generations.
Another annual highlight is the auction of blessed items, including Orh Kim (black charcoal), rice buckets and prosperity incense burners.
Cheah said Orh Kim and rice buckets remain among the most important traditional items auctioned, while proceeds from some auctions are channelled towards supporting schools and the needy.
He said the festival also plays an important role in keeping younger generations connected to the community's traditions.
"Recently, I have noticed more young people starting to participate, especially in temple affairs and worship. That is a good sign," he said.
Cheah said the festival was particularly meaningful for the neighbourhood, where it was once difficult to gather large numbers of residents for community activities.
"In the early days in Taman Bukit Maluri, it was hard to gather so many residents together, but this event brings everyone out every year.
"For me, it is a matter of faith and preserving our cultural foundation.
"Beyond faith, we preserve Chinese culture while remaining mindful and respectful of Malaysia's harmonious multiracial society," he said.
Low Kok, the association's treasurer,  said the prayer spaces prepared for devotees had already been fully occupied ahead of Monday night's ceremony.
The 61-year-old, who has served on the association's committee for 31 years, said the festival had grown alongside the neighbourhood's population, from a modest gathering when it was first organised into a major annual event for the local community.
"It started small, but as the neighbourhood population grew, our festival activities expanded alongside it," he said.
Low said preparations for the three-day festival begin about two months in advance, with committee members meeting to coordinate logistics and work with appointed sponsors.
For him, the festival also marks a personal journey with the association.
He first came to the temple to pray in 1994 and was selected as the "Lu Zhu", or Censer Master, the following year through the selection process, which led him to remain with the association ever since.
He said the festival ultimately carries hopes for the community to enjoy good health, prosperity and smooth endeavours, while also paying respects to ancestors.
"We hope each passing year will be even better than the last," he said.
[[nid:1528706]]
BRINGING THE COMMUNITY TOGETHER
As midnight approached, the temple courtyard grew increasingly crowded as devotees gathered for the final ritual of the Hungry Ghost Festival celebrations.
The atmosphere was filled with chants of "Heng Ong Huat" as devotees watched the Da Shi Ye (King of Hades) paper effigy, standing some six metres tall, being carried from the altar to the designated prayer site, alongside stacks of paper offerings prepared for the ceremony.
The chanting continued as the ritual reached its climax, with devotees offering prayers before the effigy and paper offerings were set ablaze amid cheers from the crowd.
For 46-year-old Taman Bukit Maluri resident Ryan Loo, celebrating the festival at the temple has given him a deeper appreciation of the community event.
Loo was selected as the festival's Censer Master in both 2025 and 2026 after receiving the highest number of successful "Sheng Bei" divination rituals during the selection process.
As Censer Master, Loo serves a ceremonial role, leading key prayers and rituals throughout the festival.
"For me, it is definitely a great experience. I feel fortunate to have been chosen for two consecutive years," he said.
Loo, who lives in the neighbourhood, said his experience has strengthened his belief in the importance of keeping the tradition alive within the community.
"I feel that this ceremony is something that we need to keep, prolong and extend for future generations," he said.
He said he looks forward to carrying out the rituals each year, with the hope that the prayers will bring smooth sailing and blessings to committee members and residents.
Meanwhile, for 20-year-old university student Chan Sue Ann, returning to her former neighbourhood to take part in the annual Hungry Ghost Festival is a way of staying connected to her cultural roots.
Chan, who grew up in Kepong, said she continues to return to the temple to participate in its activities despite no longer living in the area.
She said taking part in traditional Chinese celebrations gave her a sense of pride, particularly when she saw younger people helping to keep the customs alive.
"Participating in traditional Chinese events like this makes me feel especially proud.
"Seeing our Chinese traditions being preserved by the younger generation is deeply comforting and gratifying," she said.
Chan said parents could help by bringing their children to temples and involving them in different activities, allowing them to experience the traditions rather than simply learning about them.

Title: Superyacht Marina to secure Lima's future?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Genting Malaysia Bhd's planned superyacht marina can help position Langkawi as a higher-value maritime and tourism hub, while boosting its appeal to high-spending visitors.
The project, which is expected to welcome its first yachts in the second half of 2027, could also strengthen the island's case as the home of the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (Lima), industry experts said.
This comes as certain quarters have called for Lima to be moved out of Langkawi, citing constraints including accessibility, infrastructure and the island's capacity to host a larger-scale exhibition.
UniKL Business School economic analyst Associate Professor Dr Aimi Zulhazmi Abdul Rashid said the proposed marina could complement Lima's existing defence, aerospace, maritime and tourism pillars by adding luxury yachting and marine conventions.
"Adding a superyacht adds the fifth pillar which is luxury yachting or marine conventions," Aimi told Business Times.
Aimi said a superyacht marina provides Lima a permanent "show and sail" facility where naval vessels, coast guard and maritime tech exhibitors can dock all year-round.
He described Lima as the "best marketing tool" for the marina, saying the combination could help position Langkawi as a regional maritime hub.
This will transform Langkawi from a five-day event site into a 365-day maritime demo hub.
"Lima provides the global branding, the marina provides the permanent infrastructure. One without the other is weaker.
"This will strengthen the Langkawi branding as a premium tourism spot in the region. The infrastructures are already available in the well known Island," he said.
A Question Of Lima's Future
The potential synergy comes as the government weighs the longer-term future of Lima.
Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin recently said the government was exploring alternative venues, including Klebang in Melaka, if Langkawi becomes unsuitable to host the exhibition in future.
Mohamed Khaled said the move was being considered amid the need for more space and better facilities as competing defence exhibitions emerge in the region.
"Looking at Klebang, it is not far from Batu Berendam, which has an airport, and ships can also berth here. So, this is actually a location that could serve as an alternative to Langkawi.
"When Lima is held in Langkawi, not many people are able to attend. But if it is held in Melaka, people from across the country could come.
"So, this is an alternative that we can explore, although as Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said, it would require very substantial investment," he said.
Former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, meanwhile, has argued that Lima's international brand should be preserved, saying shortcomings should be addressed rather than simply moving the exhibition.
"We have spent decades building up Lima's brand at the international level, and fundamentally, it has been accepted. The presence of international defence companies is proof of this.
"If there is a major need to have another related exhibition that Lima cannot accommodate, then organise another exhibition that is more targeted," Dr Mahathir said in a post on Threads.
Marina Investment Still Under Wraps
Genting Malaysia, through Resorts World Langkawi, is partnering with Singapore-listed SUTL Enterprise Ltd's ONE°15 Marina to develop the marina, which will have more than 90 berths and accommodate superyachts of up to 140 feet.
Its location could also create a regional cruising link between ONE°15 Marina Sentosa Cove in Singapore and ONE°15 Marina Panwa Phuket in Thailand.
While Genting Malaysia has not disclosed the investment value of the proposed ONE°15 Marina Langkawi, industry estimates suggest that developing a facility capable of handling superyachts could require significant capital.
Maritime industry and logistics expert Nazery Khalid said the cost could range from US$15 million to US$65 million for a mid-sized superyacht marina, depending on the scale and specifications.
Nazery said a larger mega-destination marina built from scratch could cost between US$65 million and US$120 million, particularly if it includes integrated retail, dining, club and other lifestyle components.
He also estimated that deep-water basin dredging and wall reinforcement needed to achieve a draft of around six metres could cost between US$1 million and US$5 million, depending on tidal conditions and seabed topography.
A Regional Maritime Ecosystem
Aimi said the key question was therefore not simply whether Lima should remain in Langkawi, but whether the exhibition and new maritime infrastructure could be developed together to create a stronger year-round economic ecosystem.
"If Lima is relocated, the marina loses its biggest annual lead generator. A marina without Lima is just another marina. Together, they could be a regional maritime brand," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PuTERA35 aims to boost Bumiputera contribution
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government is exploring interventions under the Bumiputera Economic Transformation Plan 2035 (PuTERA35) to double the contribution of Bumiputera micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to Malaysia's gross domestic product (GDP) by 2035.
The proposal was among the key areas discussed at the Bumiputera Wealth Creation and Corporate Empowerment Forum held here on Monday, which focused on strengthening business growth, asset ownership and economic participation.
Bumiputera-owned businesses currently contribute 8.1 per cent to the country's GDP, with the forum examining measures to help them scale up, enhance competitiveness and create greater value and wealth.
The forum was jointly organised by Unit Peneraju Agenda Bumiputera (Teraju), Ekuiti Nasional Bhd (Ekuinas) and UDA Holdings Bhd.
It brought together representatives from the government, government-linked investment companies, government-linked companies, financial institutions, capital market players, property developers and the private sector.
Economy Minister Datuk Seri Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir, who participated in a dialogue session with forum participants, said the existing 15 per cent GDP contribution target for Bumiputera companies under PuTERA35 should not be viewed as the final goal.
"With the changing economic landscape and increasingly intense competition, we need to reassess our level of ambition and identify how Bumiputera's economic contribution can be increased.
"This requires us to build more Bumiputera companies capable of expanding at a larger scale, competing in high-value sectors and subsequently increasing Bumiputera economic participation," he said.
The forum discussed interventions to increase the scale and competitiveness of Bumiputera companies, enabling them to move beyond participation in economic value chains and become major players in high-value sectors.
Of the 11 sectors identified under PuTERA35, seven strategic sectors were identified as having significant room to increase Bumiputera participation and ownership.
These are wholesale and retail trade, halal and food, agriculture and agro-based industries, information technology, tourism, business services and logistics.
Ekuinas chief executive officer Aliff Omar Mohamad Omar said Malaysia did not lack Bumiputera entrepreneurs, but needed to help more companies grow into national and regional players.
"The bigger challenge today is how to help more Bumiputera companies grow from small and medium enterprises into national and regional-scale companies.
"Access to capital today is increasingly broad. However, sustainable company development requires more than financing alone.
"Capacity building in leadership, governance, talent and organisational management is equally important to produce more resilient Bumiputera companies capable of creating long-term value," he said.
The forum also focused on translating Bumiputera economic participation into stronger wealth ownership at the individual and household levels, as well as greater corporate ownership and control.
At the individual and household level, the focus includes increasing ownership and value of assets such as homes, property, land, equities and productive assets to build long-term wealth.
UDA chief executive officer Datuk Seri Ahmad Fuaad Kenali said Bumiputera property ownership should not be measured solely by the number of houses owned.
He said UDA would continue focusing on providing properties that meet the needs of target groups in terms of price, location, design and financing affordability
"Bumiputera assets and land need to be developed strategically so that their value continues to grow in tandem with urban development.
"We are committed to expanding ownership, increasing asset value and strengthening the Bumiputera economy, in line with the aspirations of PuTERA35," said Ahmad Fuaad.
After two years of implementation, more than 50 per cent progress has been achieved in three key drivers directly linked to the forum's agenda.
These comprise Driver 4 on wealth creation, Driver 5 on increasing equity ownership and Driver 7 on private sector, GLC and GLIC participation.
Implementation of the three drivers is targeted to reach 80 per cent by the end of 2026.
Overall, PuTERA35 is being implemented through three main pillars, 12 drivers and 132 initiatives involving ministries, agencies, GLICs and GLCs.
Its implementation is monitored by the Bumiputera Economic Council, chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Progress has also been recorded in the capital market, with three Bumiputera companies listed on Bursa Malaysia since PuTERA35 was introduced, compared with one previously.
The three companies have a combined market capitalisation of RM1.065 billion, while another two companies have received approval for listing before the end of 2026.
The developments reflect the government's efforts to strengthen financing, corporate governance, corporate readiness and access to capital markets to support Bumiputera companies' expansion.

Title: Trump seeks swift Ukraine war end, restored US-Russia ties
Article:
MOSCOW: Donald Trump told Russian President Vladimir Putin by phone on Tuesday that he wanted a swift end to the war in Ukraine, which would allow US-Russia ties to be fully restored, the Kremlin said, adding that Putin had supported the US president's view.
The call, which the Kremlin said lasted an hour, followed a weekend visit to Moscow and Kyiv by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who are trying to revive stalled talks designed to find a way to end the fighting.
Their weekend diplomacy did not appear to result in any immediate public breakthrough although they did raise the possibility that three-way talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States could be resumed. The Kremlin, which has said it does not rule that out, made no mention of the possibility in its readout of the Putin-Trump call.
Instead, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov told reporters that the two leaders had rated the US envoys' weekend diplomacy "with a plus sign" and that Putin had told Trump what he believed the United States could do to help end the conflict and given him an assessment of what the situation on the battlefield was.
Trump, Ushakov said, had made it clear he wanted the war quickly finished.
"Donald Trump clearly emphasised the desirability of bringing the conflict to an end as soon as possible, which would immediately open up prospects – impressive and far-reaching ones at that – for the full restoration of relations between the US and Russia," said Ushakov.
"In his view, this would have a particular impact on trade and economic ties, promising enormous benefits for both countries. Donald Trump is keen to see a breakthrough achieved during his presidency. Vladimir Vladimirovich Putin supported this approach."
Russia and Ukraine remain far apart on how to end the war, the deadliest in Europe since World War Two, and both sides have escalated their attacks on each other in recent months. A person close to the Kremlin, speaking before the trip by Trump's envoys, said Putin remained intent on taking full control of the remainder of the Donetsk region in eastern Ukraine, something Kyiv has vowed to continue fiercely opposing with every weapon at its disposal.
Ushakov — who said Putin and Trump had also agreed on the need to continue prisoner exchanges  — said he was not able to get into more detail about what had been discussed, but described the conversation as constructive and said the two leaders had agreed they would stay in touch and speak to each other by phone again if the need arose.
He said Putin had told Trump that Russia had no hostile intentions when it came to Europe despite repeated claims to the contrary by various European politicians.
"In light of speculation regarding Russia's alleged hostile intentions towards European states, it was emphasised that we have absolutely no aggressive plans whatsoever towards Europe," said Ushakov.
"The myths being spread about the Russian threat merely serve as a pretext for Europeans to ramp up their support for Ukraine and their own military spending," he added.

Title: Run further in Pos Malaysia Run 2026!
Article:

POS Malaysia Run 2026 is returning to Dataran Merdeka here on Nov 29.
This year, the organisers are introducing the 21km Open and Veteran categories for the third edition of the community event.
With the tagline "Jom Laju For Fun!", the event will turn the heart of the nation's capital into a lively showcase of fitness, healthy living and community spirit.
Inspired by the daily journeys of faithful postmen and couriers, who keep people and businesses connected across the country, the run will feature themes on movement, perseverance and a shared purpose.
Building on last year's turnout of more than 7,000 runners, Pos Malaysia is targeting 10,000 participants for this year's edition.

The half-marathon runs are introduced to cater to a growing base of long-distance runners.
For those aiming for a podium finish, a total of RM20,800 will be offered as prizes across all competitive categories.
Pos Malaysia Group chief executive officer Charles Brewer said the event is more than a physical challenge, describing it as an extension of the company's role and pride in connecting communities.
"The Pos Malaysia Run reflects who we are at our core, building trust, connecting communities and keeping the nation moving," Brewer said.
"Just as our Pos Wira connect people and businesses every day, this event brings Malaysians together through a shared commitment to health, well-being and community.
"Starting from Dataran Merdeka, a place rich with national significance and home to Kuala Lumpur's iconic 0km marker, makes the event especially meaningful, reminding us that every connection and every journey begins with trust," he said.
Registration is open via Race Roster (https://raceroster.com/events/2026/119344/pos-malaysia-run-2026), and closes on Sept 20.

Title: Smart mission in Nepal starts
Article:

THE Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) MAS-01 has reached Trishuli Bazar, Nepal and is preparing to begin humanitarian efforts and search for 55 Malaysians who remain uncontactable.
"The 11 members have arrived and are based at a military camp, though the name of the camp was not specified," said National Disaster Management Agency director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim yesterday.
The Smart members are expected to spend between seven and 10 days in Nepal, supporting search-and-rescue (SAR) operations in areas affected by the floods.
The team departed aboard a Royal Malaysian Air Force A400M transport aircraft from Subang on Saturday.
Meanwhile, Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Chang Lih Kang said Malaysia's rescuers had the technological expertise needed to support complex SAR operations, although he was unsure of the specific equipment deployed with the team.

Chang also stressed the importance of developing Malaysia's own technological capabilities, rather than relying on external expertise during major disasters.
He pointed to the Batang Kali landslide, where DNA analysis helped identify victims while space technology was used to detect possible subsequent landslides and improve the safety of rescue personnel.

Title: UK, France, Canada to ban imports from Israeli settlements
Article:
LONDON: Britain, France and Canada said Tuesday they will ban imports from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, with a UK minister accusing Israel of turning a blind eye to the "ethnic cleansing" of Palestinians there.
The moves prompted a furious Israel to unveil immediate counter-measures targeting Britain.
The trio of Western allies revealed the trade curbs in response to Israel's West Bank settlements policy and reports of increasing attacks by settlers there against Palestinians.
"The British government agrees that there is ethnic cleansing of Palestinians in areas of the West Bank – perpetrated by settler terrorists," said Britain's foreign minister Ed Miliband, announcing the import ban and other measures in parliament.
"All too often the Israeli government has turned a blind eye to this and worse, members of it have made statements and taken actions to support the forced displacement of Palestinians."
London, Paris and Ottawa joined nine other European countries in issuing a joint statement saying they planned to introduce or support restrictions on trade with Israeli settlements.
Within hours, Israel announced its angry response, ordering the closure of Britain's consulate in Jerusalem and banning 12 Britons from visiting the country, including lawmakers from the governing Labour party.
Israel said it would also expel British diplomats at a centre monitoring the US-brokered ceasefire plan in Gaza and bar British training for Palestinian Authority forces.
"The accusations made today by the foreign secretary in the British parliament were outrageous lies," said Israel's Foreign Minister Gideon Saar.
The settlements mainly export agricultural products, including dates, grapes, avocados, citrus fruits, and some vegetables and aromatic herbs. They also market wine, Dead Sea cosmetics and various industrial products.
Trade between the UK and the occupied Palestinian Territories was only around £38 million ($51 million) in 2025, according to the British government.
'END TRADE'
Ireland and Spain have already taken measures against trade with Israeli settlements, and France has for weeks been pushing for a similar decision from the European Union, Israel's leading trading partner, but has been blocked by some members.
Tuesday's joint foreign ministers' statement was also signed by Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Ireland, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Spain and Sweden.
They said "unprecedented levels of settler violence and settlement expansion" in the West Bank threatened prospects for a two-state solution to the conflict.
The E1 settlement plan – approved by Israel last year after decades of being frozen – would see 1,200 housing units built and further isolate Israeli-annexed east Jerusalem from the rest of the West Bank.
Addressing MPs flanked by new Prime Minister Andy Burnham, Miliband – the son of Jewish immigrant parents – also vowed "action against specific companies and individuals who provide services such as construction, infrastructure, financing, or real estate for settlement expansion."
In a statement posted on X, French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said France "will end trade" with settlements in the occupied territories.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the United States would not join the new sanctions, saying Washington does not want to destabilise the West Bank.
TOUGHENING UK STANCE
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed to continue establishing the settlements – illegal under international law.
Israel has already faced intense international criticism over its relentless offensive that flattened much of Gaza following the Oct 7, 2023, attack on Israel by Hamas.
The UK government's move and hardening rhetoric signals a toughening of its stance towards Israel under Burnham, who replaced Keir Starmer in July.
Starmer's government last year formally recognised a Palestinian state and announced sanctions on selected entities.
More than 500,000 Israelis live in illegal settlements in the West Bank, among some three million Palestinians.
According to an AFP tally based on data from the Palestinian health ministry, Israeli forces or settlers have killed at least 1,105 Palestinians in the territory since the start of the Gaza war.

Title: Social media firms that flout 'duty of care' face hefty Aussie fines
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
SOCIAL MEDIA giants face A$109 million fines if they fail to protect young users from harmful content, said Australia's prime minister yesterday as he unveiled draft laws reining in big tech.
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese released draft laws that would place a "duty of care" on the firms behind popular platforms such as Facebook, TikTok and Instagram.
Social media companies would be held responsible for protecting under-18s from pornography, online bullying, content that glorified crime and content that encouraged eating disorders.
"We took action because the community said 'enough is enough'. We would no longer let Australian kids be treated as commodities instead of children."
Social media firms face mounting scrutiny over their use of allegedly addictive algorithms and stand accused of directing users to extreme content to keep them scrolling.
The draft laws build on Australia's world-first social media ban for under-16s, which came into effect late last year.
Companies found to be flouting their "duty of care" could be fined up to A$109 million, said Albanese.
The legislation includes a requirement that platforms allow users to "opt out" of powerful algorithms that determine what comes up on social media feeds.
"This will give Australians greater choice over their platforms and what they see."
It would require firms like Meta, which owns Facebook and Instagram, to give users the option of turning off algorithms that tailor recommendations to their personal taste.
Communications Minister Anika Wells said yesterday big tech was facing a "reckoning".
"Their platforms and tools have infiltrated our daily lives in ways that we could never have imagined. Some good, but some with terrible consequences," she said.
Data last month found that under-16s in Australia were increasing their use of social media apps such as Instagram and TikTok despite the ban.
The draft laws would be introduced to parliament later this year after consultation with social media companies, industry bodies and civil society groups. — AFP

Title: Doctor killed in helicopter crash returned to Sarawak just two days ago - Father
Article:
KOTA BARU: Dr Ainul Baraah, who was killed in a helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Sarawak, had returned to the state just two days ago after spending a week on holiday with her family in Kelantan.
"My daughter had only returned to Sarawak two days ago after spending a week here. Today, we received news that the helicopter she was travelling in had crashed and that she had died," Kamaruddin Salleh, 69, said when contacted.
He said Ainul, the fourth of five siblings, had been working as a doctor on a permanent basis for about two years and was attached to a hospital in Miri.
"Initially, I received a call from my in-law informing me that the helicopter she was on had crashed and that her condition was still unknown.
"Later, I received a second call informing me that my daughter had died.
"My wife, Rogayah Mohd Noor, 69, was devastated upon receiving the news and we were at a loss for words.
"My wife and I have yet to travel to Sarawak as she is unwell and has existing health problems," he said.
He said his other children and his in-laws' family would fly to Kuala Lumpur before continuing their journey to Sarawak tomorrow morning.
Describing Ainul as a quiet and kind-hearted daughter, Kamaruddin said she often helped the family.
"During her week back in the village, Ainul took us out several times," he said.
Earlier, a Bo-105 helicopter carrying five people, including the pilot, was reported to have
crashed near the Long Lellang STOL port
in Sarawak this afternoon.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) confirmed the incident in a statement.
CAAM said it received notification of the incident from the Aeronautical Information Service at 3.58pm.

Title: Azeez Rahim detained ahead of graft charges, says son
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri  Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim has been detained by Dang Wangi police ahead of an expected remand, his son said.
Azeez's son, Azman Azeez, said in a Facebook post that his father was supposed to appear at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court tomorrow to face graft charges.
"Tomorrow was also supposed to be the day he would join his fellow comrades at the Umno General Assembly. But tonight, all those plans have changed," he said.
"I do not want to pre-empt the court process. Nor do I want to judge anyone. I only hope that this process will be conducted fairly, transparently and without prejudice. A charge is only a charge until it is proven in court," he said.
A check of the court system showed that Azeez, a former Baling member of parliament, is
scheduled to be charged
before Judge Azura Alwi at 9am tomorrow.
On Aug 27, Azeez and former Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Mohd Irwan Siregar were each remanded for seven days, until Sept 2, to assist investigations following disclosures related to the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the institution.
Both men are being investigated under Section 23(1) of the MACC Act 2009.
The RCI report on Tabung Haji, published on July 29, recommended, among other measures, a forensic audit to examine past investment decision-making that led to a significant decline in the institution's asset value.
Azman said his father was once again in custody, this time at the Dang Wangi police station, and was expected to be remanded tomorrow.
"Tomorrow, my father was supposed to appear at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court to face charges that were to be brought against him.
"I only ask everyone reading this… Please pray for my father. Pray that Allah gives him strength, peace and protection. Pray that everything will be made easier for him.

Title: Bersatu Padang Besar rocked as members from 14 branches quit party
Article:
PADANG BESAR: Members from 14 of the 24 Bersatu branches in Padang Besar have quit the party with immediate effect, effectively crippling the division.
Padang Besar Bersatu deputy chief Ramzi Md Udi said the decision was made after they lost confidence in the party's central leadership.
He said the mass resignations were reached through a consensus following discussions with division and branch leaders as well as their respective committee members.
"Today, members representing 14 of the 24 branches announced their decision to quit the party. This means more than two-thirds of Bersatu branches in Padang Besar have been dissolved, and several more branches are expected to follow suit.
"The decision was made after careful consideration. We no longer have confidence in the division, state and central leadership," he said at a press conference tonight.
Also leaving the party were division deputy chief Ramli Aripin, acting division Srikandi chief Fazuwin Razak and division Srikandi Muda chief Nurul Hafiza Ramli.
Ramzi said the group had also agreed to continue their political struggle by joining Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan), led by Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin.
"For a clearer political future and in the interest of the people, we have chosen to move forward by joining Wawasan," he said.
Ramzi also claimed that the appointment of Izizam Ibrahim as the new Perlis Bersatu chairman appeared to signal an agenda to further strain ties with Pas in the state.

Title: NST Leader: Scammers are evolving, the law must keep up
Article:
THERE is an unwritten rule  that sensible Malaysians live by when they receive calls on their smartphones. If the call is from an unknown number, especially with a foreign  country code, the receiver would ignore or summarily reject it.
For most Malaysians, this common-sense  response is the first line of defence against  scam calls.    Still, some people, especially vulnerable citizens, forget this rule.
This is when scam callers strike, using  psychology, charm and voice hypnosis to convince their gullible victims to do the unthinkable.   Like giving up logins, passwords, personal details and bank account numbers under bogus "threats of police action".   Before they know it, victims lose their life savings to scammers who then vanish, leaving no digital trail.
Last year, 73 per cent of surveyed Malaysians admitted to being deceived by various scams, but most common were recorded phone scams, with 28,388 cases.
Over several years, police investigated 8,011 cases that resulted in losses of RM440 million, RM4,844.70 being the average single loss.   Across various digital and phone channels, 66,204 cases were recorded as cyber fraud surged nationwide.
Here's the rub: three in four adults can spot scams, yet educated and digitally savvy millennials remain targeted.   Online scam victims then turn to the police for help but, troublingly, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail lamented that current laws were struggling to keep pace with the criminals.
The National Scam Response Centre receives 500 to 600 complaints daily, a figure that justifies tougher laws.   Unfortunately, arrests seem pointless if the eventual punishment cannot sufficiently deter organised criminal networks.
The IGP's criticism of the Computer Crimes Act 1997, which is meant to be the vanguard against cyber scams,  is pertinent: it is a law  radically out-of-step with current digital scams.
Artificial intelligence-generated voices, deepfakes, social engineering and professional operations haven't been met with updated laws that align with the latest technological advancements.   Moreover, scammers realise that the rewards vastly outweigh the punishment.
Police have proven they can arrest syndicate members repeatedly but the "manageable" convictions are simply the cheaper cost of doing business for criminals.
Enforcement needs sophisticated technology, skilled white hat hackers, investigative powers and inter-agency cooperation to identify global perpetrators.
Here's a suggestion: introduce corporal punishment like caning, lengthy imprisonment, higher fines and asset forfeiture.
Let's see if  scammers can take punishment that's usually reserved for drug trafficking and sexual assault — anything to make scamming highly unattractive.
Apart from the foot soldiers, target syndicate organisers, financiers, mule-account operators and launderers of illicit proceeds.   Eventually, the goal is to destroy the entire racket.

Title: US sanctions threaten to crush Iranian students' dreams
Article:
SHE had planned to study psychology in Italy, but after United States sanctions forced the suspension of an English exam required in order to make her dream come true, Iranian student Nikki cried for days.
Nikki had been due to take the TOEFL English proficiency test, a key qualification required by many foreign universities, in Iran later this month.
Now, like many Iranian students dreaming of a future elsewhere, she is scrambling to find another way to take it, while absorbing the new exam fee and hefty travel costs.
Testing has been frozen in Iran following the latest US sanctions announced last month, part of Washington's "economic asphyxiation" of the country over the Middle East war.
"When I found out that the exam had been cancelled... I did not leave my room for several days because I was crying," said the 32-year-old, who works at a pastry shop in the northern city of Lahijan.
"My plans were left hanging midway."
The US-based Educational Testing Service (ETS), which administers the TOEFL English proficiency test, said the exams were suspended after the US Treasury stopped issuing licences for them.
On its website, ETS said Iranians could still travel abroad to take the exams.
Alternatives, including the PTE English proficiency test and the increasingly popular Duolingo online exam, have also been suspended, according to Iranian media.
"We can no longer take any of the exams here," said Nikki.
But taking the exams abroad is scarcely affordable for many Iranians.
Millions have already been struggling for decades under international sanctions, with economic pressures compounded by more than six months of war with the US.
The rial has plunged to record lows, reaching around 2.2 million to the US dollar in recent days, while year-on-year inflation hit 89 per cent for the Iranian month ending Aug 22, sharply eroding purchasing power.
"I am now trying to get a loan so that I can book the exam and go to a neighbouring country to take it," said Nikki, adding that she was considering Armenia.
"The money I was supposed to spend on the health of my teeth now must go towards the exam and the trip," she added.
In Telegram groups sharing updates and advice about the tests, students were scrambling to find the cheapest and quickest alternatives to complete their applications.
In one group with more than 24,000 members, users weighed travelling to neighbouring Armenia, Iraq or Turkiye, while others calculated the mounting costs.
One contributor ruled out taking the exam in Istanbul, saying "going there is for the rich who can afford flights".
Iranian officials have condemned the suspension, saying the restrictions showed that Washington was targeting "every Iranian citizen in every field".
Science Minister Hossein Simaei Saraf slammed the move as "'Stone Age' behaviour", an apparent reference to language used by US President Donald Trump when he threatened to send Iran back to the Stone Age.
For Leila, a 32-year-old Teheran resident, news of the cancellations was another blow after she secured a place in a graduate arts programme in Berlin this summer.
She had already deferred her university offer for a year because of uncertainty surrounding the war, which has persisted despite an April ceasefire that halted its most intense phase.
"I have no plans to take the exam elsewhere; financially, it is not possible for me to take it outside Iran," she said, describing the "sheer despair" among Iranians hoping to study abroad.
With her plans in disarray, Leila said she would probably pursue further study inside Iran instead.
"I have learnt to make several plans to survive tough situations," she said. "So I will probably go to university here."
The writers are from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: How 2 men survived 9 days in hydropower tunnel after Nepal floods
Article:
A DELIRIOUS  Kabir Maharjan drifted in and out of consciousness in a pool of muddy water in complete darkness, trapped for nine days in a tunnel beneath the wreckage of Nepal's worst flood disaster in decades.
He was one of hundreds of hydropower workers believed to have been buried when a glacier collapsed above Nepal's Trishuli valley on Aug 26, unleashing a wall of mud and water that killed more than 1,300 people and left thousands missing across Nepal and neighbouring Tibet.
He and mechanical foreman Sanjay Sah survived in an air-filled chamber, said lawmaker Shri Ram Neupane, a veteran tunnel engineer who helped lead the rescue effort.
At 7.30am on the day of the disaster, Maharjan called his wife before his shift at the Upper Trishuli 3A hydropower project.
"I have to go inside the tunnel," he told her. "There won't be any network inside."
Around 60 minutes later, a glacier collapsed at the Langtang Lirung mountain some 40km upstream, causing a landslide so powerful that it formed a wall of water that flattened villages and submerged a network of 12 hydropower projects with nearly 900 workers inside.
In Kathmandu, electricity department officials were monitoring the projects' power supplies on their screens. Then the fields started going blank — one after another.
Suraj Dahal, an engineer at the Nepal Electricity Authority who led parts of the rescue effort, said he was not immediately alarmed because "floods are normal" in the country.
They soon understood otherwise. At 9.15am. — two minutes after Maharjan's wife, Hira Shova Maharjan, had tried and failed to reach him — officials gave the final order to 3A: "Evacuate!"
Sah, who worked in the power house's control room, sped from floor to floor, warning colleagues individually, he later said.
Of the tunnel's four access routes, engineering drawings seen by Reuters showed one ran more than 180m to the underground powerhouse — but rescuers believed it was flooded, offering no hope of survivors.
Maharjan and Sah had taken shelter just 160m from the exit — "at the corner, at the edge of the tunnel", as Maharjan would later describe it to his wife.
For the next nine days, the air pocket that had saved their lives became their prison.
Serious digging didn't start until three days after the disaster. All four tunnels were blocked — mud, rock, timber and debris, some of it buried under 15m to 30m of landslide material.
A breakthrough came when a 12.7cm borehole drilled from above finally confirmed the tunnel's true alignment, giving crews a fixed point to dig.
It took rescuers nearly six days just to reach the tunnel's buried entrance, said Amshu Kiran Shahi, a board member of the Nepal Electricity Authority.
When they called out for survivors, nobody answered.
At 4am on the 10th day, Dahal got a call from a heavy equipment operator: the rescuers had heard something.
Ganga Baral, who led the rescue team, said they began to hear noises as they drilled into the tunnel.
"We would call out, 'Where are you? Are you there?'" said Baral. "Sometimes it felt like there was a person alive trying to communicate with us."
They still couldn't make out words — but they now estimated the source was just 15m to 20m away. Then, in the beam of a light, they saw a hand.
Another 5m to 10m of mud-choked passage stood between them and the survivor.
By 7am, soldiers broke open a small hole. From inside came a single word: "hunuhuncha", which loosely translates to "we are here".
Neither man could stand when rescuers finally pulled them from the tunnel.
Sah, his face caked in mud, had to be carried out on a rescuer's back. He managed to lift one hand towards a camera.
Maharjan, with more severe injuries, went out on a stretcher.
At the hospital, doctors operated on a deep, infected wound on Maharjan's leg, said his wife.
When Hira Shova walked into the hospital room, he did not recognise her.
"Where am I?" he asked her.
But she was just thrilled to get him back alive.
"He is blessed with another life."
The writers are from Reuters

Title: Five media workers lose contact while covering Anak Krakatau eruption
Article:
JAKARTA: Five Indonesian media personnel reportedly lost contact while covering the eruption of Mount Anak Krakatau near Sebesi Island, Lampung, southern Sumatra, not far from the volcano, today.
Banten Search and Rescue (SAR) Office Chief Al Amrad said the joint SAR team was still conducting an intensive search operation to locate all the media personnel.
"Search and rescue teams are still searching for the five media personnel who lost contact. As of tonight, there is still no information on whether they have been found," he said in a statement today.
The five media personnel are Muhammad Bagus Khoirunnas from Indonesia's national news agency Antara; Arie Basuki from news portal Merdeka.com; Yudistiro Pranoto from iNews; Firdaus Wajidi from Türkiye's Anadolu Agency; and Donal Husni, a freelance journalist.
In addition to the five media personnel, three boat crew members travelling with them — Warta, 55; Surakman, 60; and Heriyanto, 49 — were also unreachable, bringing the total number of missing people on board to eight.
They were reported to have departed from Anyer in Banten, at the western tip of Java Island, on Monday aboard a speedboat bound for the Krakatau area to cover the volcano's eruptive activity.
Mount Anak Krakatau is located in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra islands and has experienced a series of eruptions over the past few days, causing volcanic ash to spread to several areas in western Indonesia and disrupting flight operations.
According to the latest information, Al Amrad said the last communication with the group was made through Muhammad Bagus, a photographer with Antara's Banten Bureau, at around 4pm yesterday before they could no longer be contacted.
Following this, he said the National Search and Rescue Agency (Basarnas) deployed teams to Sebesi Island and the Mount Anak Krakatau area for the search operation today.
He said SAR teams are searching land and sea areas across Sebesi Island and near Mount Anak Krakatau for any trace of the five media personnel.

Title: Pilot's wife asks for prayers after Sarawak heli crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The wife of pilot Captain Zainol Afiq has asked for prayers for her husband after the Long Lellang helicopter crash today.
Izzati Syamimi posted on Threads: "Pray for me and my children. Pray for my husband, my heaven."
Five people, including the pilot, were on board the Bo-105 helicopter, which was operating the Health Ministry's Flying Doctor Service to the Sarawak interior.
Several social media users also posted messages of support and condolences on Izzati's Threads post.
@amirthaqiff wrote: "My condolences, Mimi. InshaAllah, may he (Zainol) be granted a place in heaven. Capt Zainol was a good person. I personally knew him from flying school."
Another user, Fazeera_ilyas said: "Stay strong sis. Your children need their mother very much."
Stnrlrznh said: "My condolences, sis. May Allah ease all your affairs and grant strength and resilience to Kak Mimi and her children."
Meanwhile, in a separate post, @_.aimansUhaimi called on the public to recite Al-Fatihah for all the crew, including his brother-in-law.
He said his sister and her children were already at Miri airport with his brother-in-law's colleagues.
Earlier today, the BO-105 helicopter carrying five people, including its pilot, crashed near the Long Lellang STOLport in Sarawak.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia said it received notification of the incident from the Flight Information Service at 3.58pm.
Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah said police have mobilised a search and rescue (SAR) team following the crash, however said the status of all those on board, including the pilot, was still under investigation.
Zainal said the SAR team will head to the location, which will take 10 hours by road from the Marudi district police headquarters.
